topStories.headline: SF Opera Orchestra Threatens Opening-Night Strike; Opera Ball Moved to November
topStories.dek: Contract negotiations between the San Francisco Opera and its orchestra musicians have thrown the season's gala into uncertainty, forcing Opera Ball off its September 12 date — though Simon Boccanegra's opening-night curtain still stands.
topStories.body:
San Francisco Opera's annual Opera Ball, one of the Bay Area's most prominent fall galas, will not take place on its planned September 12 date after the orchestra warned it would not perform without a new collective bargaining agreement by opening night. <cite index="110-3,110-4">San Francisco Opera announced its 2026 Opera Ball is delayed; originally scheduled for September 12 at San Francisco City Hall, the Opera Ball will now take place on November 12.</cite>

<cite index="110-5,110-6">The season-opening performance of Verdi's 'Simon Boccanegra' at the War Memorial Opera House will continue as planned on September 12 without the gala component of the evening. The date change follows the recent announcement by the San Francisco Opera Orchestra of their intention not to perform unless the Opera and Orchestra have resolved a new collective bargaining agreement by opening night of the season.</cite>

<cite index="116-7,116-12">The orchestra's previous contract expired on July 31. Meanwhile, the orchestra said it wants a contract providing 'stability and pay that keeps pace with the cost of living in this city,' as well as a plan to expand the company's schedule, lengthen runs of popular productions and grow its audience.</cite> <cite index="116-13">"We are not walking away from the table," the musicians said.</cite>

<cite index="111-1">Six performances of Simon Boccanegra are scheduled for September 12 (8 p.m.), 16 (7:30 p.m.), 19 (2 p.m.), 22 (7:30 p.m.), 25 (7:30 p.m.), and 27 (2 p.m.).</cite> <cite index="116-11">Music Director Eun Sun Kim is set to conduct an international cast led by baritone Amartuvshin Enkhbat, soprano Eleonora Buratto, bass-baritone Christian Van Horn and tenor Joshua Guerrero.</cite> Tickets remain on sale at sfopera.com.

topStories.headline: Supervisors Advance $38.9M OpenGov Permit Contract; Full Board Vote Set for September 15
topStories.dek: A key City Hall committee unanimously cleared Mayor Lurie's controversial software deal on September 2, but stopped short of endorsing it, setting up a contentious full Board of Supervisors vote.
topStories.body:
<cite index="38-7,38-8">A Board of Supervisors committee on Wednesday unanimously approved extending a contract worth up to $38.9 million for OpenGov, a controversial software that Mayor Daniel Lurie has championed as part of his efforts to overhaul the city's clunky permitting system. The 3-0 vote by the Budget and Finance committee cleared one of the final hurdles for the city to all but lock in OpenGov as its go-to permitting software for the next half-decade.</cite>

<cite index="44-1,44-2">Supervisors scrutinized Lurie's plan Wednesday to push through an extension contract with OpenGov for the city's PermitSF platform while questioning the portal's performance and the administration's decision to bypass competitive bidding. The Board of Supervisors' Budget and Finance Committee advanced the proposal to keep OpenGov on as the technology provider for PermitSF, but stopped short of recommending that the full board approve the proposed five-year, $33 million extension. PermitSF is intended to replace San Francisco's notoriously fragmented permitting infrastructure.</cite>

<cite index="27-4,27-5">Almost a year ago, Mayor Daniel Lurie's office awarded a $5.9 million contract for an ambitious overhaul of the city's archaic permitting system to OpenGov, a largely untested tech firm with connections to his former nonprofit, Tipping Point. This occurred without a formal bidding process, and over the objections of departmental staff.</cite> <cite index="27-7,27-8">Since then, OpenGov has missed key deadlines by several months to roll out basic permits. The software Lurie championed still has limited functionality and, city workers say, is still only being applied to simpler tasks.</cite>

<cite index="44-5,44-6">Supervisor Jackie Fielder, who requested a legislative analysis and previously called for a hearing on the procurement process, said she supports the goal of creating a unified permitting system but questioned whether the city received the best deal. "I am, however, questioning whether we got the best deal for this contract, and for the people of San Francisco," Fielder said.</cite> <cite index="37-12">The full Board of Supervisors is expected to vote on the request on September 15.</cite>

topStories.headline: Tenderloin Museum Holds Annual Gala at War Memorial After June Fire Closes Its Doors
topStories.dek: A fire at the Cadillac Hotel above the Tenderloin Museum in June forced the institution to close; its 11th annual gala on September 23 will be held at the War Memorial Green Room as the museum pursues repairs and fundraising.
topStories.body:
<cite index="127-17,127-18">A fire on June 27 forced the Tenderloin Museum to close, the museum reported. The fire originated 'in the residential floors of The Cadillac Hotel, above our space.' The museum has launched a fundraising drive.</cite>

<cite index="127-1,127-2">The Tenderloin Museum's 11th Annual Gala, titled 'A Decade Plus One,' is set for September 23 from 5 to 8:30 p.m. The gala is particularly important this year given the June fire that closed the main venue for repairs.</cite> <cite index="126-2">It will be held at the Green Room at San Francisco War Memorial, 401 Van Ness Ave.</cite>

<cite index="126-15,126-16,126-17">The museum's 11th Annual Gala brings together supporters for a night of live entertainment, community voices, and distinctive food and drink. Eleven years ago, the Tenderloin Museum opened its doors in one of San Francisco's most misunderstood neighborhoods with a simple but radical idea: that the Tenderloin's stories deserved to be told with dignity, depth, and pride. Over the last decade, the museum has grown into a living, breathing cultural institution that is reshaping how this city sees itself.</cite>

<cite index="126-18">Last year, the museum marked its 10th anniversary by breaking ground on a $3.7 million expansion project that will triple its physical space over the next two years.</cite> <cite index="126-9,126-10">Gala attendance supports the exhibitions, productions, and community programs that make the museum essential, and ensures that the Tenderloin's story continues to be told by the people who lived it, on their own terms, in their own neighborhood.</cite> Tickets are available via Humanitix at the museum's website.

events.title: wave to earth at Bill Graham Civic Auditorium

events.description: <cite index="91-1,91-2">The South Korean indie-pop band wave to earth plays the Bill Graham Civic Auditorium on Tuesday, September 8, with doors at 7:15 p.m. and show at 8:15 p.m. This event is all ages.</cite> The show is sold out; resale tickets remain available.

events.title: SF Symphony: Samara Joy with the SF Symphony
events.location: Davies Symphony Hall, 201 Van Ness Ave, Civic Center
events.description: <cite index="48-5">Grammy-winning jazz vocalist Samara Joy joins conductor Anthony Parnther and the Symphony for an evening featuring jazz standards and original songs</cite> to kick off the SF Symphony's 115th season.

events.title: SF Opera: Simon Boccanegra — Season Opening
events.location: War Memorial Opera House, 301 Van Ness Ave, Civic Center
events.description: <cite index="111-2,111-3">San Francisco Opera's 2026–27 season begins September 12 with Music Director Eun Sun Kim leading an international cast in Giuseppe Verdi's Simon Boccanegra. Last seen on the War Memorial Opera House stage in 2008, the opera will be presented in Claus Guth's production from the Hamburg State Opera.</cite> Note: Opera Ball has been postponed to November 12 due to ongoing orchestra contract negotiations.

events.title: Live on Larkin: Little Saigon 51st Anniversary Block Party
events.description: <cite index="59-6,59-7">Celebrate the 51st Anniversary of Little Saigon at Live on Larkin, a huge neighborhood celebration packed with live performances, fashion shows, karaoke, delicious food, and performances by Circus Bella.</cite> <cite index="59-8">Live on Larkin is part of Welcoming Week in SF.</cite> Free to attend.

events.title: SF Symphony: Opening Gala with Hilary Hahn
events.location: Davies Symphony Hall, 201 Van Ness Ave, Civic Center
events.description: <cite index="48-1">The Symphony officially opens its new season on September 24 with its annual Opening Gala, led by conductor Giancarlo Guerrero and featuring superstar violinist Hilary Hahn performing Mendelssohn's Violin Concerto.</cite> <cite index="48-2">During the concert, the Symphony will present the Ellen Magnin Newman Award to Cultura y Arte Nativa de las Americas (CANA), recognizing the organization's more than four decades of preserving and celebrating Latino, Caribbean, and African diasporic cultural traditions in the Bay Area.</cite>

events.title: Tenderloin Museum 11th Annual Gala: 'A Decade Plus One'
events.location: The Green Room, San Francisco War Memorial, 401 Van Ness Ave
events.description: <cite index="128-1,128-2">The Tenderloin Museum's 11th Annual Gala brings together supporters for live entertainment, community voices, distinctive food and drink, and an opportunity to connect with Tenderloin enthusiasts, set against the backdrop of The Green Room at San Francisco War Memorial.</cite> The museum has been closed since a June fire; the gala doubles as a fundraiser toward repairs and its ongoing $3.7 million expansion. Register via Humanitix.

events.title: Civic Center Soundtrack — Free Lunchtime Concerts
events.location: Fulton Plaza, Civic Center (Fulton St at Larkin St)
events.description: <cite index="13-14">The Civic Center Soundtrack returns for its third season starting Tuesday, April 14, 2026, bringing live music to Fulton Plaza twice a week through October.</cite> Concerts run Tuesdays and Thursdays from noon to 3 p.m. and are free.

moreNews.headline: New Exhibition Opens at SF Main Library September 4, Running Through January 2027
moreNews.body: <cite index="76-9">A new exhibition opens Friday, September 4, 2026, at the Main Branch of the San Francisco Public Library and runs through Thursday, January 21, 2027, with hours from 1:00 to 5:00 p.m.</cite> The Main Library at 100 Larkin Street is closed Monday, September 7, for Labor Day but otherwise maintains its regular schedule. Check sfpl.org for the full exhibition title and programming details.

moreNews.headline: Larkin Street Revival Gains Momentum as New Businesses Open in Little Saigon Corridor
moreNews.body: <cite index="56-15,56-16,56-17">A new bookstore/café has opened on Golden Gate between Hyde and Larkin, businesses backed by OEWD grants are opening on Larkin, and a Mexican restaurant is even opening at the long drug-challenged southwest corner of Ellis and Jones.</cite> The activity is part of the Larkin Street Revival project, funded by a <cite index="57-9">$5 million investment from crypto billionaire and philanthropist Chris Larsen, co-founder of payment network Ripple.</cite> <cite index="56-20,56-21">Overall, the Tenderloin's sidewalk drug use has declined in 2026, with two of the three previously worst blocks — Hyde and Eddy and the 100 block of Leavenworth — showing improvement.</cite>

restaurants.name: Sungho

restaurants.name: Villon
restaurants.description: All-day restaurant inside the San Francisco Proper Hotel serving seasonal California cuisine in a Kelly Wearstler-designed space with artistic flair.

restaurants.name: Charmaine's

hotels.name: The Tilden Hotel

hotels.name: Civic Center Motor Inn

shops.name: Heart of the City Farmers Market
shops.description: A year-round outdoor farmers market at United Nations Plaza offering fresh produce, specialty foods, and prepared items from Bay Area growers, held Wednesday and Sunday mornings.

shops.name: Asian Art Museum Store

shops.name: SF Main Library Wednesday Used Book Sale
shops.description: Every Wednesday, the Larkin Street steps of the SF Main Library host a browseable used book sale spanning all genres; free and open to all.

shops.description: An ongoing artisan gift gallery at Fulton Plaza selling handcrafted goods from local makers as part of the Civic Center public space activation program.

shops.name: Onsen SF
shops.description: A Japanese-inspired bathhouse in the Tenderloin offering communal mineral soaking baths, private rooms, and rotating dinner pop-ups in an intimate setting.

gymsRecreation.name: Onsen SF
